note: For each situation I wrote the premise first as ordinary prose, then built the neutral member by finding the inference a reader would silently carry away from it — continuation of a habit, completion of an intention, the cause behind a stated fact — and checked each one by asking whether it could be false with every word of the premise still true.

cases.premise: The bakery on Wren Street opened its doors at five every morning through the winter of 2019.
cases.hypothesis: The Wren Street bakery was opening at five in the morning during the winter of 2019.

cases.premise: The bakery on Wren Street opened its doors at five every morning through the winter of 2019.
cases.hypothesis: The Wren Street bakery did not open until midday that winter.

cases.premise: The bakery on Wren Street opened its doors at five every morning through the winter of 2019.
cases.hypothesis: The Wren Street bakery still opens at five in the morning.
cases.why_plausible: Shops are assumed to keep the hours they have always kept, so a reader carries the 2019 routine forward to today without noticing.

cases.premise: Nadia handed in her thesis on the last Friday of March, a full two weeks before her department's deadline.
cases.hypothesis: Nadia handed in her thesis before her department's deadline.

cases.premise: Nadia handed in her thesis on the last Friday of March, a full two weeks before her department's deadline.
cases.hypothesis: Nadia handed in her thesis after her department's deadline had already passed.

cases.premise: Nadia handed in her thesis on the last Friday of March, a full two weeks before her department's deadline.
cases.hypothesis: Nadia had been working on that thesis for more than a year.
cases.why_plausible: Theses are long pieces of work, so a reader assumes a stretch of years behind the submission rather than a few concentrated months.

cases.premise: Until last April the ferry to Kestrel Island ran twice a day; since then it has run on Saturdays only.
cases.hypothesis: The Kestrel Island ferry runs less often now than it did before last April.

cases.premise: Until last April the ferry to Kestrel Island ran twice a day; since then it has run on Saturdays only.
cases.hypothesis: The Kestrel Island ferry still makes two crossings every day.

cases.premise: Until last April the ferry to Kestrel Island ran twice a day; since then it has run on Saturdays only.
cases.hypothesis: The twice-daily crossing to Kestrel Island had been running for many years before it was cut back.
cases.why_plausible: The word "until" makes the old schedule sound long-established, though the premise is equally consistent with its having started only months earlier.

cases.premise: Theo and Ruth Okonkwo are siblings who grew up in the same house in Leeds; Ruth is four years older than Theo.
cases.hypothesis: Ruth is the elder of the two Okonkwo siblings.

cases.premise: Theo and Ruth Okonkwo are siblings who grew up in the same house in Leeds; Ruth is four years older than Theo.
cases.hypothesis: Theo is the elder of the two Okonkwo siblings.

cases.premise: Theo and Ruth Okonkwo are siblings who grew up in the same house in Leeds; Ruth is four years older than Theo.
cases.hypothesis: Theo and Ruth have the same mother and the same father.
cases.why_plausible: Siblings raised under one roof and sharing a surname read as full siblings, but half-siblings and step-siblings are described the same way.

cases.premise: For eleven years Dolores Marchetti lived next door to the Farrells, and she looked after their cat whenever they went away.
cases.hypothesis: Dolores Marchetti and the Farrells were next-door neighbours for eleven years.

cases.premise: For eleven years Dolores Marchetti lived next door to the Farrells, and she looked after their cat whenever they went away.
cases.hypothesis: Dolores Marchetti never lived anywhere near the Farrells.

cases.premise: For eleven years Dolores Marchetti lived next door to the Farrells, and she looked after their cat whenever they went away.
cases.hypothesis: Dolores Marchetti and the Farrells were friends.
cases.why_plausible: Years of looking after a neighbour's cat sounds like friendship, though it can equally be a paid or merely civil arrangement between people who are not close.

cases.premise: Ingrid Vance wrote to her old schoolteacher, Mr. Osei, every Christmas for twenty years, and he wrote back each time.
cases.hypothesis: Ingrid Vance and Mr. Osei exchanged letters across a span of twenty years.

cases.premise: Ingrid Vance wrote to her old schoolteacher, Mr. Osei, every Christmas for twenty years, and he wrote back each time.
cases.hypothesis: Mr. Osei never once answered Ingrid Vance's letters.

cases.premise: Ingrid Vance wrote to her old schoolteacher, Mr. Osei, every Christmas for twenty years, and he wrote back each time.
cases.hypothesis: Ingrid Vance and Mr. Osei met in person at least once during those twenty years.
cases.why_plausible: A warm correspondence lasting two decades with a former teacher makes a visit or a chance meeting feel almost certain, yet the premise records only letters.

cases.premise: The watercolours hanging in the hallway were painted by Amira Delacroix, who marks her work with a small blue heron.
cases.hypothesis: The hallway watercolours are the work of Amira Delacroix.

cases.premise: The watercolours hanging in the hallway were painted by Amira Delacroix, who marks her work with a small blue heron.
cases.hypothesis: The hallway watercolours were painted by someone other than Amira Delacroix.

cases.premise: The watercolours hanging in the hallway were painted by Amira Delacroix, who marks her work with a small blue heron.
cases.hypothesis: Amira Delacroix paints professionally.
cases.why_plausible: A painter with her own signature device sounds like someone who sells and exhibits, but keen amateurs adopt such marks too.

cases.premise: The crime novels published under the name Rowan Ash were all written by Beatriz Alonso, a retired magistrate from Seville.
cases.hypothesis: Beatriz Alonso is the author of the crime novels that appear under the name Rowan Ash.

cases.premise: The crime novels published under the name Rowan Ash were all written by Beatriz Alonso, a retired magistrate from Seville.

cases.premise: The crime novels published under the name Rowan Ash were all written by Beatriz Alonso, a retired magistrate from Seville.
cases.hypothesis: Beatriz Alonso drew on her years on the bench when she wrote those novels.
cases.why_plausible: A magistrate turned crime novelist invites the assumption that the courtroom fed the fiction, though she may have written about something else entirely.

cases.premise: The runner who crossed the line first in the Saltcoats ten-mile was Priya Raman; her twin sister Meena came ninth.
cases.hypothesis: Priya Raman won the Saltcoats ten-mile.

cases.premise: The runner who crossed the line first in the Saltcoats ten-mile was Priya Raman; her twin sister Meena came ninth.
cases.hypothesis: It was Meena Raman who crossed the line first at Saltcoats.

cases.premise: The runner who crossed the line first in the Saltcoats ten-mile was Priya Raman; her twin sister Meena came ninth.
cases.hypothesis: The two Raman sisters are often mistaken for one another at races.
cases.why_plausible: Twins running the same races suggest constant confusion, but twins can look nothing alike and the premise says nothing about their resemblance.

cases.premise: Since 2021 Devon Achebe has run the scheduling desk at the Northgate dental clinic, although he has no clinical training of any kind.
cases.hypothesis: Devon Achebe is not a trained clinician.

cases.premise: Since 2021 Devon Achebe has run the scheduling desk at the Northgate dental clinic, although he has no clinical training of any kind.
cases.hypothesis: Devon Achebe treats patients at the Northgate clinic.

cases.premise: Since 2021 Devon Achebe has run the scheduling desk at the Northgate dental clinic, although he has no clinical training of any kind.
cases.hypothesis: Devon Achebe answers to the clinic's senior dentist.
cases.why_plausible: In a small clinic the dentist is imagined at the top of everything, though an administrator can just as easily report to a practice manager or owner.

cases.premise: Hannah Wexler directs the Barrow Vale community choir: she picks the programme each season and takes the Tuesday rehearsals.
cases.hypothesis: The Barrow Vale choir's seasonal programme is chosen by Hannah Wexler.

cases.premise: Hannah Wexler directs the Barrow Vale community choir: she picks the programme each season and takes the Tuesday rehearsals.
cases.hypothesis: Hannah Wexler has no say in what the Barrow Vale choir performs.

cases.premise: Hannah Wexler directs the Barrow Vale community choir: she picks the programme each season and takes the Tuesday rehearsals.
cases.hypothesis: Hannah Wexler stands in front of the Barrow Vale choir at its concerts.
cases.why_plausible: Whoever chooses the music and runs the rehearsals is naturally pictured on the podium, yet choirs often bring in a guest conductor for the performance itself.

cases.premise: On the Ellisfield bridge project, Marta Kubik was the foreman who signed off each day's concrete pours.
cases.hypothesis: Signing off the daily concrete pours at Ellisfield was Marta Kubik's job.

cases.premise: On the Ellisfield bridge project, Marta Kubik was the foreman who signed off each day's concrete pours.
cases.hypothesis: Marta Kubik held no authority over the concrete work at Ellisfield.

cases.premise: On the Ellisfield bridge project, Marta Kubik was the foreman who signed off each day's concrete pours.
cases.hypothesis: Marta Kubik was the most senior person on the Ellisfield site.
cases.why_plausible: A foreman with sign-off authority sounds like the person in charge, though engineers and project managers routinely sit above the foreman on a bridge job.

cases.premise: Since he retired, Gerald Vance has swum at the lido on Mondays and Thursdays.
cases.hypothesis: Gerald Vance gets to the lido at least twice in an ordinary week.

cases.premise: Since he retired, Gerald Vance has swum at the lido on Mondays and Thursdays.
cases.hypothesis: Gerald Vance has not set foot in the lido since he retired.

cases.premise: Since he retired, Gerald Vance has swum at the lido on Mondays and Thursdays.
cases.hypothesis: Gerald Vance goes to the lido on no days other than Mondays and Thursdays.
cases.why_plausible: Naming two days invites the reader to hear them as the complete list, although nothing in the sentence rules out an extra swim on a Saturday.

cases.premise: The Okarie family has kept a vegetable stall at the Thursday market in Ashcombe for six years, missing only the weeks when the market itself was cancelled.
cases.hypothesis: The Okaries have been at the Ashcombe market on nearly every Thursday for six years.

cases.premise: The Okarie family has kept a vegetable stall at the Thursday market in Ashcombe for six years, missing only the weeks when the market itself was cancelled.
cases.hypothesis: The Okaries have turned up at the Ashcombe market only once or twice in all that time.

cases.premise: The Okarie family has kept a vegetable stall at the Thursday market in Ashcombe for six years, missing only the weeks when the market itself was cancelled.
cases.hypothesis: The Okaries also sell their vegetables at markets in other towns.
cases.why_plausible: Market traders are assumed to work a circuit of towns rather than live off one morning a week, but the premise mentions only Ashcombe.

cases.premise: Dr. Solveig Haugen is called out at night perhaps three or four times a month, usually to the farms north of the village.
cases.hypothesis: Night call-outs are not an everyday event for Dr. Haugen.

cases.premise: Dr. Solveig Haugen is called out at night perhaps three or four times a month, usually to the farms north of the village.
cases.hypothesis: Dr. Haugen is called out on very nearly every night of the month.

cases.premise: Dr. Solveig Haugen is called out at night perhaps three or four times a month, usually to the farms north of the village.
cases.hypothesis: Dr. Haugen is the only doctor serving the farms north of the village.
cases.why_plausible: One named country doctor doing the night rounds reads as the sole doctor for miles, though she may simply be one of several sharing the rota.

cases.premise: The Brennans put their house on Calder Road up for sale in September, hoping to settle nearer their daughter in Cork.
cases.hypothesis: The Brennans wanted to end up living closer to their daughter.

cases.premise: The Brennans put their house on Calder Road up for sale in September, hoping to settle nearer their daughter in Cork.
cases.hypothesis: The Brennans had no wish to live any nearer their daughter.

cases.premise: The Brennans put their house on Calder Road up for sale in September, hoping to settle nearer their daughter in Cork.
cases.hypothesis: The Brennans have since moved to Cork.
cases.why_plausible: A plan reported in the past tense feels like a plan that came off, but a house can sit unsold and the move never happen.

cases.premise: Tomás Iglesias applied for the joinery apprenticeship at Hallward & Sons because he wants a workshop of his own one day.
cases.hypothesis: Tomás Iglesias has an ambition to run his own workshop.

cases.premise: Tomás Iglesias applied for the joinery apprenticeship at Hallward & Sons because he wants a workshop of his own one day.
cases.hypothesis: Tomás Iglesias has no interest in ever running a workshop of his own.

cases.premise: Tomás Iglesias applied for the joinery apprenticeship at Hallward & Sons because he wants a workshop of his own one day.
cases.hypothesis: Hallward & Sons gave Tomás the apprenticeship.
cases.why_plausible: We are told about the application as though it mattered, which makes the reader supply a successful outcome the sentence never gives.

cases.premise: Miriam Stanek drafted a long letter of complaint to the water company, meaning to send it once she had collected her neighbours' signatures.
cases.hypothesis: Miriam Stanek wanted her neighbours' signatures on the letter before it went off.

cases.premise: Miriam Stanek drafted a long letter of complaint to the water company, meaning to send it once she had collected her neighbours' signatures.
cases.hypothesis: Miriam Stanek intended to post the letter with no signatures on it at all.

cases.premise: Miriam Stanek drafted a long letter of complaint to the water company, meaning to send it once she had collected her neighbours' signatures.
cases.hypothesis: The letter reached the water company in the end.
cases.why_plausible: A determined complainant with a finished draft seems bound to post it, yet the signatures may never have been gathered and the letter never sent.

cases.premise: Ayo Bankole was visibly nervous before he gave the graduation address, stopping twice to steady his hands.
cases.hypothesis: Ayo Bankole's nerves were plain to anyone watching him before the address.

cases.premise: Ayo Bankole was visibly nervous before he gave the graduation address, stopping twice to steady his hands.
cases.hypothesis: Ayo Bankole showed no trace of nerves before the address.

cases.premise: Ayo Bankole was visibly nervous before he gave the graduation address, stopping twice to steady his hands.
cases.hypothesis: Ayo Bankole felt relieved once the address was behind him.
cases.why_plausible: Relief is the expected sequel to stage fright, though he might have come off feeling ashamed of how it went, or nothing much at all.

cases.premise: When her old collie died in February, Frances Doyle gave up her usual walks along the towpath.
cases.hypothesis: Frances Doyle's collie died in February.

cases.premise: When her old collie died in February, Frances Doyle gave up her usual walks along the towpath.
cases.hypothesis: Frances Doyle's collie was still alive in the spring.

cases.premise: When her old collie died in February, Frances Doyle gave up her usual walks along the towpath.
cases.hypothesis: Frances Doyle was grieving for the collie.
cases.why_plausible: Abandoning a daily walk after a pet dies reads as mourning, though the simple fact that there was no longer a dog to walk would explain it just as well.

cases.premise: Karel Novak laughed and wept at once when his brother came through into the arrivals hall at Ostrava after eleven years abroad.
cases.hypothesis: Karel Novak was in tears at the sight of his brother in the arrivals hall.

cases.premise: Karel Novak laughed and wept at once when his brother came through into the arrivals hall at Ostrava after eleven years abroad.
cases.hypothesis: Karel Novak was unmoved when his brother came through into the arrivals hall.

cases.premise: Karel Novak laughed and wept at once when his brother came through into the arrivals hall at Ostrava after eleven years abroad.
cases.hypothesis: Karel Novak had been counting the days until his brother came home.
cases.why_plausible: Such a reunion suggests long anticipation, but the return may have been sudden news and the feeling entirely of the moment.

cases.premise: Paula Ferreira joined the Kettlebridge rowing club in 2018 and still pays her subscription every January.
cases.hypothesis: Paula Ferreira is a subscription-paying member of the Kettlebridge rowing club.

cases.premise: Paula Ferreira joined the Kettlebridge rowing club in 2018 and still pays her subscription every January.
cases.hypothesis: Paula Ferreira has never belonged to the Kettlebridge rowing club.

cases.premise: Paula Ferreira joined the Kettlebridge rowing club in 2018 and still pays her subscription every January.
cases.hypothesis: Paula Ferreira rows with the Kettlebridge club most weekends.
cases.why_plausible: Someone who keeps paying is assumed to be out on the water, though lapsed members go on renewing out of loyalty or habit for years.

cases.premise: Every driver at the Arden depot except two belongs to the transport union.
cases.hypothesis: Not all of the Arden depot's drivers are union members.

cases.premise: Every driver at the Arden depot except two belongs to the transport union.
cases.hypothesis: All of the drivers at the Arden depot belong to the transport union.

cases.premise: Every driver at the Arden depot except two belongs to the transport union.
cases.hypothesis: The transport union bargains over pay on behalf of the Arden drivers.
cases.why_plausible: Near-total membership makes collective bargaining the obvious purpose, yet the employer may not recognise the union at that depot at all.

cases.premise: The Thursday book group at Milford library has nine members, one of them Owen Blaise, who has been with it since it began in 2005.
cases.hypothesis: Owen Blaise is one of the nine members of the Milford Thursday book group.

cases.premise: The Thursday book group at Milford library has nine members, one of them Owen Blaise, who has been with it since it began in 2005.

cases.premise: The Thursday book group at Milford library has nine members, one of them Owen Blaise, who has been with it since it began in 2005.
cases.hypothesis: Owen Blaise founded the Milford book group.
cases.why_plausible: The longest-standing member is easily mistaken for the founder, though he may simply have come along to the first meeting somebody else called.

cases.premise: The basement of the Alderney Hotel flooded after a water main burst under the street outside during January's cold snap.
cases.hypothesis: The flooding of the Alderney Hotel basement followed the bursting of the water main.

cases.premise: The basement of the Alderney Hotel flooded after a water main burst under the street outside during January's cold snap.
cases.hypothesis: The Alderney Hotel basement stayed dry when the main gave way.

cases.premise: The basement of the Alderney Hotel flooded after a water main burst under the street outside during January's cold snap.
cases.hypothesis: It was the cold that made the water main burst.
cases.why_plausible: Frost is the standard explanation for a winter burst, but the sentence places the cold snap alongside the failure without blaming it, and old pipes fail in any weather.

cases.premise: The Tiverton orchard lost most of its apple crop that year; a late frost in May had killed the blossom.
cases.hypothesis: A late frost in May killed the blossom in the Tiverton orchard.

cases.premise: The Tiverton orchard lost most of its apple crop that year; a late frost in May had killed the blossom.

cases.premise: The Tiverton orchard lost most of its apple crop that year; a late frost in May had killed the blossom.
cases.hypothesis: The Tiverton orchard finished that year out of pocket.
cases.why_plausible: A ruined crop sounds like a ruinous year, though insurance, stored fruit or a higher price on what survived could have carried the orchard through.

cases.premise: The fire in the trawler's engine room started when a fuel line chafed through where it ran against a bracket.
cases.hypothesis: A fuel line that had chafed through was what started the fire in the engine room.

cases.premise: The fire in the trawler's engine room started when a fuel line chafed through where it ran against a bracket.
cases.hypothesis: The fuel line had nothing to do with the start of the engine-room fire.

cases.premise: The fire in the trawler's engine room started when a fuel line chafed through where it ran against a bracket.
cases.hypothesis: The fuel line had been run incorrectly when the engine was installed.
cases.why_plausible: A line rubbing on a bracket sounds like sloppy installation, though a correctly fitted line can shift over years of vibration and heavy seas.

cases.premise: At six, Jonah Whitlock could not get through a sentence unaided; by the end of the following year he was working his way through chapter books on his own.
cases.hypothesis: Jonah Whitlock's reading improved over the course of that year.

cases.premise: At six, Jonah Whitlock could not get through a sentence unaided; by the end of the following year he was working his way through chapter books on his own.

cases.premise: At six, Jonah Whitlock could not get through a sentence unaided; by the end of the following year he was working his way through chapter books on his own.
cases.hypothesis: Jonah Whitlock was given extra help with his reading during that year.
cases.why_plausible: So sharp a turnaround invites the reader to supply a tutor or a special programme, although children often simply come to reading late and then all at once.

cases.premise: Marrowfield was a village of four hundred people in 1970; today some nine thousand live there and the old lanes have disappeared under new estates.
cases.hypothesis: Marrowfield holds far more people now than it did in 1970.

cases.premise: Marrowfield was a village of four hundred people in 1970; today some nine thousand live there and the old lanes have disappeared under new estates.

cases.premise: Marrowfield was a village of four hundred people in 1970; today some nine thousand live there and the old lanes have disappeared under new estates.
cases.hypothesis: Most of Marrowfield's growth came from people moving out of the nearby city.
cases.why_plausible: New estates round a village are read as commuter overspill, but the premise never says where the nine thousand came from.

cases.premise: After the accident Sefton Mbeki could not stand without help; eight months later he walked the length of the hospital corridor on his own.
cases.hypothesis: Sefton Mbeki got back the ability to walk without help.

cases.premise: After the accident Sefton Mbeki could not stand without help; eight months later he walked the length of the hospital corridor on his own.
cases.hypothesis: Sefton Mbeki never walked unaided again after the accident.

cases.premise: After the accident Sefton Mbeki could not stand without help; eight months later he walked the length of the hospital corridor on his own.
cases.hypothesis: Sefton Mbeki made a full recovery from his injuries.
cases.why_plausible: Walking again is read as the end of the story, though a corridor on one's own is a long way short of recovering everything that was lost.
